findings.problem: UILoader_ResolveViewIndexById's lookup chain is less fully specified than UILoader_BuildSelectorFromMarkup's. It says 'uses the side table / host views' and returns an index (<0 when unresolved) but does not spell out the id -> side-table row -> container pointer -> host->views index chain explicitly.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to §6 stating UILoader_ResolveViewIndexById resolves the id through the same side-table container-identity path as §5 step 1, returning a negative sentinel for an unmatched id (mapped to index 0 by §7 step 10).

findings.problem: The freshly built selector is left at active_index == count (unselected sentinel) until the mandatory ViewHostSystem_SelectView call. This is safe but not called out as index-safe.
findings.fix: Optionally note that UpdatePanelViewSelectorButtons uses active_index only in an equality test (i == active_index), never as an array index, so the count sentinel causes no out-of-bounds access. Matches AllocatePanelViewSelector's existing active_index = count initialisation.

findings.location: Design §5 / Error handling (allocation failure in UILoader_BuildSelectorFromMarkup)
findings.problem: The design says to 'mirror AllocatePanelViewSelector's cleanup', but both AllocatePanelViewSelector and DestroyPanelViewSelector are static to view_host_system.c and not callable from ui_loader.c.
findings.fix: State explicitly that the loader open-codes the cleanup with the public Deallocate: Deallocate(&buttons, sizeof(UIElement*)*count), Deallocate(&view_indices, sizeof(int)*count), Deallocate(&selector, sizeof(ViewSelector)) — because DestroyPanelViewSelector is not visible to the loader. Behaviour as described is already correct.
